Work list

Private residence · 14 jobs · 13 September 2026

Everything we’d like done, in the order that matters to us — the first group first, and the rest as time allows. No need to get through all of it in one visit.

A couple of things worth knowing up front: 4 of the 14 are electrical, and items 9 and 10 run in sequence — the brick pad has to go down before the storage unit can be built on it. Both are ready to go: the bricks and the unit are already here.

Start with these

The ones that matter most.

4High

Fix side-gate latch + add locks to both side doors

Exterior / hardware

The side-gate latch hardware is worn/rusty and needs replacing. The replacement latch has already been bought — labour only, no parts needed for the latch itself. Also add lock options to BOTH side doors/gates.

5High

Fix broken wall air vent (register)

HVAC / general

The wall HVAC vent cover/register is detached and hanging off the wall — needs reattaching or replacing.

9High

Lay bricks to make a flat pad for the storage unit

Landscaping / hardscape

Level the dirt and lay bricks to create a flat, stable base for the outdoor storage unit — the strip along the fence shown in the photo. The bricks have already been bought, so this can go ahead immediately. Needs to be genuinely level: resin boxes flex on uneven ground and the lid stops closing properly. Measure the carton on site before laying — it is roughly 68in x 32in, so allow about 72in x 36in of pad plus room to stand in front with the lid open.

10High

Assemble the storage unit on the new pad

Assembly / general

Build the outdoor storage box on the brick base. The unit has arrived and is still boxed — see photo. Needs item 9 done first. It is a large resin deck box, roughly 68in long x 32in deep x 34in tall; exact figures are on the carton.

Note from us: ASKPASS 360 gallon resin deck box. Assembly instructions are inside the box.
See the box on Amazon — full listing and photos
https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0H7MCTKNF

2Medium

Electrical

Install lighting at the front entrance.

3Medium

Backyard and backdoor lighting — inspect existing, hang solar string lights

Electrical

Two parts, same job. First, inspect the backdoor lights, both the solar ones and the hanging ones. Second, hang a solar string light set across the deck seating area — see the photo, it is the area under the shade sail, with runs up into the surrounding trees. The lights have already been bought (a string of bulbs, solar), so there is nothing to source, and being solar there is no wiring and no power supply needed. There is already a tensioned cable across the deck holding the shade sail, plus tree anchor points, which may save putting in new fixings. A sunny spot for the solar panel has already been identified, so the shade over the seating area is not a problem.

7Medium

Dark water stain on the hardwood floor

Flooring / refinishing

Roughly circular dark stain on the oak floor where slime was left sitting. Water has gone through the finish into the timber and reacted with the tannin, so it is in the wood rather than on it. Present for over a week, so it is fully dry — this is a settled stain, not surface residue. The pale flecks in the photo are from attempting to scrape it off. Likely needs oxalic acid (wood bleach) or a spot sand and refinish, with blending to the surrounding boards.

11Medium

Hoses — tighten all connections, untwist the one at the back

Exterior / hardware

All hose connections need tightening so they stop leaking. Separately, the hose at the back is twisted and needs sorting out.

15Medium

Pop the window screen back into the office window

Exterior / hardware

The office window screen is out and needs refitting. It should simply pop back into the frame — likely a few minutes rather than a job in its own right, so worth bundling into the same visit.

16Medium

Run an electrical cable to the deck for an outlet

Electrical

Mount an electricity cable out to the deck so there's a power outlet there. Outdoor-rated outlet and cable, and the run needs to be fixed rather than trailing. Exact position on the deck to be shown on site.
